column1: #mapping_set_title: "CFIHOS V2.0 property dictionary to IFC4 ADD2 property and quantity machinery"

#comment: "SCOPE, STATED UP FRONT: the open CFIHOS OWL exposes a PROPERTY DICTIONARY, 1,388 classes such as 'shell wall thickness' and 'upper limit design pressure', not a labelled equipment taxonomy in owl:Class form. So this is a crosswalk at the PROPERTY layer and nowhere else, and an equipment-class crosswalk between CFIHOS and IFC is not authorable from the open artefacts. THE FINDING: CFIHOS names 1,388 process-plant properties; IFC names roughly a dozen generic quantity and property constructs. The mapping is therefore MANY-TO-ONE INTO A GENERIC SLOT. Going CFIHOS to IFC loses the name and keeps the number; going IFC to CFIHOS is not determined at all. That asymmetry is the plant-to-building handover problem stated exactly. Exact normalised token overlap between the two class sets is ONE name. CFIHOS is an IOGP publication; this references the Universidad de Murcia OWL rendering and restates no IOGP material. Confidence is the curator's judgement."

column9: Worked example of the general pattern. A CFIHOS length property lands in IFC as a generic length quantity, so the value and its unit survive and the CFIHOS name does not. The round trip is lossy: from IfcQuantityLength alone you cannot recover which of the 100-plus CFIHOS length properties this was.

Second worked example, and the collision is the point: 'wall thickness', 'nominal wall thickness', 'shell wall thickness', 'tube wall thickness' and 'lower limit wall thickness' are five distinct CFIHOS properties that all map to the same IFC construct.
Third of the colliding set above, recorded explicitly so that the many-to-one collapse is visible in the data rather than only argued in prose.
Fourth of the colliding set. In CFIHOS the qualifier 'shell' carries real engineering meaning about which part of a vessel is measured; IFC has nowhere to put it except a free-text property name.

The nearest thing to a genuine cross-domain property, since buildings insulate too. Even here IFC would normally carry it in a material-layer property set rather than as an element quantity, so the target is arguable.

Nominal diameter is the single most-used identifier of piping components in process plant. IFC has no nominal-size concept and reduces it to a length quantity, discarding the fact that a nominal size is a designation rather than a measurement.

Pressure has no IFC quantity type at all: IfcElementQuantity covers length, area, volume, weight, count and time. So every one of CFIHOS's 180-plus pressure properties degrades to a generic named property value in a property set, outside the quantity machinery entirely.
Second pressure example, kept to show that design and operating conditions, a distinction CFIHOS treats as fundamental, collapse into indistinguishable property values on the IFC side.

A regulatory classification under the Pressure Equipment Directive, drawn from a controlled list. IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue is the right IFC construct for a value from a list, but IFC carries no such list and no notion that the classification is regulatory.

As above for hazardous-area classification. Hazardous-area data is safety-critical in process plant and has no IFC representation beyond an untyped enumerated property, which is worth knowing before relying on a handover.

The route worth using. Because the Murcia rendering already grounds every CFIHOS property in IDO, and this repository certifies ido:QualityDatum against ifc:IfcPhysicalQuantity with a reasoner, CFIHOS reaches IFC through IDO as a hub rather than by direct mapping. Composing two certified hops beats authoring 1,388 direct ones.

The other half of the hub route, for the 772 CFIHOS classes grounded on ido:Quality rather than ido:PhysicalQuantity. Weaker because IfcProperty straddles the borne characteristic and its recorded value, a distinction IDO keeps and IFC does not.

ASSERTED NON-MAPPING against the equivalence reading of the first row. narrowMatch is correct and exactMatch is not: promoting any of these rows to equivalence would make every CFIHOS length property equivalent to every other, since they would all be equivalent to the same IFC class. The many-to-one shape must not be promoted to OWL.

ASSERTED ABSENCE. IFC's quantity set has no pressure member, so no pressure property has a quantity-level target. Recorded once against a representative property to make the gap machine-visible rather than inferable only by reading the schema.

ASSERTED ABSENCE. Flow rate is a rate, and IFC quantities are static magnitudes of an element. Process behaviour, which is most of what CFIHOS records about operating equipment, has no home in IFC's quantity model at all.
